18. As observed during the trial test, the fire spread rapidly and severely along the re-entrant. The temperature on 1/F, 2/F and 3/F rose to 60°C after 30m 34s (1834s), 27m 13s (1633s), and 27m 4s (1624s) respectively.2 The wooden board on 2/F was ignited by the intense fire in the re-entrant, which in turn spread through the opening on 2/F into the staircase void, with the peak temperature recorded immediately outside the wooden board reaching approximately 1,000°C eventually. This extreme heat, combined with the vigorous fire spread, likely caused conditions in the lift lobbies, corridors and staircases connecting to the re-entrant to deteriorate rapidly in the actual fire incident, thereby severely impeding evacuation efforts during the fire at Wang Fuk Court. Therefore, it is reasonable to assume that the lift lobbies, corridors and staircases at Wang Fuk Court became untenable as the rapid fire spread along the re-entrant was observed.

Untenable Conditions during the Early Stages

19. To fully convey the hostile environment that developed during the early stages of the fire at Wang Fuk Court, the following observations are provided alongside supporting photographs and captures of CCTV. These findings illustrate the rapid onset of untenable conditions, driven by toxic smoke throughout the corridors, lift lobbies, and staircases at various buildings, as well as the blockage of entrances/exits by collapsed burning scaffoldings. They showcase the extreme and life-threatening situations faced by anyone trapped inside these buildings at the early stage of the incident, residents and workers alike.
